saints.name: St. Benjamin
saints.title: Deacon and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A Persian deacon who would not stop preaching the Gospel and was martyred with cruel torture under King Bahram V…
biography: Benjamin was a deacon of the Persian church during the forty years of persecution that began under King Yazdegerd I and raged more fiercely under his son Bahram V. Imprisoned for a year for the faith, he was released through the intercession of an ambassador of the Roman emperor Theodosius II, on condition that he preach Christ no more.

Benjamin answered that he could not be silent about Christ. Seized again, he was put to tortures recorded by the church historian Sozomen: sharpened reeds were driven beneath the nails of his hands and feet and into the tenderest parts of his body, and at last a knotty stake ended his sufferings, about the year 424.

His constancy under such torments made him one of the most renowned martyrs of the Persian church. The Roman Martyrology keeps his name on 31 March, and the churches of East and West alike venerate him as a martyr of Christ.
saints.knownFor: Refusing to be silent about the Gospel, unto martyrdom.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
